workstream.name: pkg
workstream.unlocks: Milestone 6 pkg-cli: after `pkg.sync` materializes a format-1 lock and immutable store entries, ordinary CLI evaluation can resolve package modules by name with ECL_PATH unset.

problemStatement: Milestone 4 can fetch, verify, unpack, and lock source packages, but the runtime loader still knows only embedded modules and ECL_PATH. A synchronized project therefore cannot execute its locked dependencies by package name, and adding an implicit fetch to evaluation would violate the workstream's reproducibility and authority boundary.
solutionSummary: Add an opaque, immutable ProjectLock snapshot that Session creates once from the first upward-discovered ecl.pkg and its sibling ecl.lock when the host explicitly supplies a project-start path. AutoLoadDriver will consult that snapshot after embedded lookup and before ECL_PATH, incrementally select the longest owning package prefix, and derive the store candidate from the selected package key plus the requested module's full canonical filename. A matched package is authoritative: absent store state and malformed locks become structured language errors, while an absent lock or unmatched name preserves the legacy path. The implementation stays source-only, performs no network or lock mutation, and retains the existing loading lease, racing-winner recheck, cycle detection, and poll budget.

mergabilityStrategy.featureFlagStrategy: No feature flag is needed. The CLI opts ordinary execution into discovery with Host.project_start, while the library default remains null; even in an opted-in session the new tier is inert when upward discovery finds no ecl.pkg or the sibling ecl.lock is absent. Patch 3 is the only behavior patch and delivers the complete coherent tier.
mergabilityStrategy.patchOrderingStrategy: Patches 1 and 2 are independent INFRA patches: one fixes the written runtime contract and one lands compiling skipped acceptance cases. Patch 3 depends on both, implements and enables every case in the same commit as the production wiring, and is the sole BEHAVIOR patch.

currentStateAnalysis: HEAD includes the four completed package milestones through commit a9318d5: format-1 ecl.pkg/ecl.lock readers and writers, pure MVS, bounded archive/TLS host capabilities, pkg.sync, immutable store keys, and atomic lock publication. AutoLoadDriver in src/machine.zig currently acquires the module loading lease, rechecks for a racing winner, checks stdlib.find, and then moves directly to ECL_PATH filename construction; every import, qualified operand, load-only observation, and completion-triggered cold load converges on that driver. Session already owns optional host capabilities and copies them into unit.inherited, but it has no project-discovery input or lock snapshot. M4's archive contract stores root-level files by full canonical module name (for example foo.bar.ecl), so the M5 workstream phrase that derives a candidate from the prefix remainder must be corrected rather than implemented literally.

operationalConsiderations.externalSystemAccess: The new runtime path adds no external service and must never invoke the existing HTTP/TLS capabilities. It reads only local ecl.pkg/ecl.lock metadata and immutable package-store directories through std.Io during Session initialization and module loading. src/main.zig supplies project_start = "." for ordinary CLI execution; embedders and in-process tests remain opted out unless they deliberately provide a start path and host I/O.
operationalConsiderations.crossRuntimeContracts: Milestone 4's ECL runtime is the producer of canonical format-1 ecl.lock files and immutable store keys; this gameplan's Zig ProjectLock is the independent consumer. Patch 3 must validate the same format, name/prefix rules, selected package/version/url/hash fields, cache-root precedence (ECL_CACHE, then XDG_CACHE_HOME/ecl/pkg, then HOME/.cache/ecl/pkg), and `<package>-<version>-<lowercase-sha256>` key derivation. Compatibility tests use locks written through the public package vocabulary rather than a private Zig-only representation.
operationalConsiderations.failureBehavior: No marker, no sibling lock, no host I/O, or a null project_start disables the tier and leaves legacy resolution unchanged. A malformed or unreadable sibling lock is captured in the one-time snapshot and reported as a structured ECL error on the first non-embedded lookup, so embedded modules remain available and Session initialization keeps its OOM-only API. Once a valid lock owns a module prefix, failure is fail-closed: a missing cache root/store entry names the package and instructs `ecl pkg sync`; a missing source file names the package and module; neither condition falls through to ECL_PATH or the network. Oversized lock traversal and prefix matching advance through bounded cursors and ordinary OOM propagation.
operationalConsiderations.concurrencyAndIdempotency: ProjectLock is immutable and Session-owned; inherited units receive only an opaque observation capability that cannot mutate the lock, store, allocator, or reclamation domain. AutoLoadDriver acquires the existing loading lease and performs the racing-winner recheck before starting the lock cursor, so concurrent requests retain the existing single-publication and cycle semantics. Lock scanning and candidate construction consume the established kernel poll budget, and any heap state held across pending phases is owned with heap.Owned. Repeated resolution reads the same snapshot and immutable store path and is idempotent.
operationalConsiderations.rollbackStrategy: This milestone writes no project or store state and changes no on-disk format. Reverting Patch 3 removes the consumer while leaving M4-produced locks and immutable store entries valid and inert; legacy embedded/ECL_PATH loading resumes immediately. There is no migration, compensating write, or cleanup step.

functionalChanges.description: An opted-in Session walks upward from Host.project_start once, selects the first ecl.pkg, snapshots its sibling ecl.lock, and otherwise preserves legacy behavior when the marker, lock, host I/O, or opt-in is absent.

Module resolution order is embedded module, then the valid lock's longest owning dotted-package prefix, then ECL_PATH for unmatched names; a locked candidate uses the requested module's full canonical filename inside the selected immutable store entry.
Imports, qualified execution, load-only observation, and cold completion can publish and use source modules from a synchronized locked package with ECL_PATH unset.

A matched package prefix is authoritative: a missing store entry names the package and tells the user to run `ecl pkg sync`, and a missing module file names both module and package, with no ECL_PATH fallback.
A malformed or unreadable sibling lock remains hidden from embedded lookup but produces one deterministic structured language error before any ECL_PATH lookup for a non-embedded module.
Runtime lock resolution is read-only and source-only: it never reaches HTTP/TLS, fetches a package, mutates ecl.lock, or accepts native artifacts.
Concurrent requests for one locked module still converge through the existing loading lease, racing-winner recheck, cycle detection, single publication, and bounded scheduler polling.

contextResources.why: Milestone 5 defines tier order, discovery, read-only resolution, concurrency preservation, TSan evidence, terminal acceptance ownership, and the M6 boundary. Its remainder-path sentence must be reconciled with the already-landed M4 archive contract.

M1 is authoritative for strict format-1 validation, dotted prefix ownership, upward project discovery, the sibling lock location, source archive layout, and the requirement that the independent Zig and ECL readers agree.

M4 fixes cache precedence, immutable store-key spelling, canonical lock production, exact archive roots, and atomic publication. M5 must consume those artifacts without inventing a second storage layout.

These files are the verified live path from CLI/Session entry through root-unit inheritance, module loading arbitration, embedded lookup, ECL_PATH candidate transfer, and registry publication. Patch 3 must change this path rather than add a parallel loader.

These are the public runtime, concurrency/TSan, initialized-Session OOM, built-binary, source-classification, allocator-policy, and test-tier seams required by the repository policy. Existing name-prefix routing already places loader tests in precommit and concurrency tests in workers/TSan.

The repository contract requires opaque authority, one lifetime protocol, bounded user-sized work, owner-after-descendant teardown, explicit structural documentation, exhaustive classification, and real publication-path concurrency proof.

The workstream already selected these precedents for separating lock consumption from network mutation, content-addressed package layout, layered runtime/package tooling, and dotted-prefix package ownership.

acceptanceCriteria: With ECL_PATH absent, the built CLI started below a synchronized project root imports and executes a source module from the immutable store selected by ecl.lock.
Embedded stdlib modules win over a colliding locked package; among locked packages the longest dotted prefix wins; unmatched names retain legacy ECL_PATH behavior.
The store candidate is `<cache>/<package>-<version>-<hash>/<full.requested.module>.ecl`, matching M4's root-level archive layout.
Session reads project metadata once from the first upward-discovered ecl.pkg and sibling ecl.lock; changing the file afterward does not retarget that Session.
Null project_start, absent host I/O, no marker, or no sibling lock produces byte-identical embedded/ECL_PATH behavior.

Malformed lock, missing locked store entry, and missing locked module are deterministic structured errors; matched packages never fall through, and the missing-store error names the package and `ecl pkg sync`.
Runtime evaluation performs no network access, lock write, package fetch, or native artifact load.
Concurrent locked loads publish once through the production loading lease and registry path; the Linux/x86_64 `zig build test-tsan` gate is green.
The smallest locked discovery/load path is included in the initialized-Session OOM sweep, and every new source is exhaustively classified.
Each new test is first proven capable of failing, then restored; `zig build precommit` passes with stdin closed under timeout.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Library sessions do not read ambient project state by default
explicitOpinions.rationale: Host.project_start is an explicit borrowed capability and defaults to null; src/main.zig supplies "." for the CLI. This preserves hermetic embedders/tests, keeps no-host behavior exact, and still implements the workstream's process-cwd discovery rule for the product entry point.

explicitOpinions.opinion: A valid matched package prefix is authoritative
explicitOpinions.rationale: Falling through to ECL_PATH when a selected store artifact is absent would let local files silently shadow the lock and destroy reproducibility. Unmatched names may still use ECL_PATH; matched names report the responsible package and recovery action.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Locked candidates use the full requested module filename
explicitOpinions.rationale: M4 accepts source archives with root-level canonical filenames such as foo.bar.ecl. Deriving bar.ecl from the remainder after package foo would make M5 unable to consume the artifacts M4 deliberately validates and stores.

explicitOpinions.opinion: ProjectLock is one opaque Session-owned snapshot with a bounded lookup cursor
explicitOpinions.rationale: An opaque capability prevents units from forging allocator/domain correlations or mutating package state; one immutable snapshot makes concurrent resolution deterministic. The cursor keeps user-sized lock and prefix traversal inside the scheduler's polling contract.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Invalid-lock state is captured at initialization and materialized on non-embedded lookup
explicitOpinions.rationale: Session initialization currently exposes only OutOfMemory, while the evaluator already owns structured language errors. Delaying only error materialization preserves that API and embedded precedence without rereading the lock or falling through to ECL_PATH.

changes: Implement ProjectLock as an opaque allocation with a factory that walks parents from project_start, stops at the first ecl.pkg, reads its sibling ecl.lock at most once, strictly validates format 1, and owns either immutable selections or an owned deterministic failure until deinit.

Accept cache environment inputs through a narrow CacheInputs value rather than importing machine.Environ or accepting a correlated allocator/domain tuple; reproduce M4 cache precedence and exact immutable store-key spelling.

Implement LookupCursor as bounded, pollable longest-prefix work over canonical dotted names. Return match metadata only; construct `<store-key>/<full-module-name>.ecl`, never a suffix-only path or native candidate.

Add Host.project_start = null, copy/resolve it during Session initialization when host I/O exists, own ProjectLock in SessionCore, carry `?*const ProjectLock` on InheritedContext, and deinitialize it after scheduler descendants and before allocator teardown.

Extend AutoLoadDriver's tagged phase state after the racing-winner and stdlib checks. Keep the loading cursor/lease and cycle result untouched; hold lookup and candidate allocation across polls with heap.Owned, and raise authoritative invalid-lock/missing-store/missing-module errors without ECL_PATH fallback.

Measure Frame after adding the nominal owned phase state; if it exceeds the existing 104-byte ceiling, raise and explain that ceiling instead of weakening the ownership type or splitting correlated raw fields.
Opt only src/main.zig's ordinary execution and REPL into project discovery with `project_start = "."`; leave Session library defaults and unrelated formatter paths ambient-resource-free.

Implement every pending test using explicit temporary paths, no ambient stdin/network/wall clock, and public runtime/executable outcomes. For each new test, deliberately break one assertion, run its owning tier to observe failure, restore it, then run with stdin closed and an immediate captured status.

Extend the initialized-Session OOM probe with the smallest fixture that reaches discovery, strict lock parsing, lookup, candidate construction, and source publication; do not add a separate expensive Session bootstrap.

Run `timeout 500 zig build precommit < /dev/null` with status captured immediately. Because loader timing changes, also run the repository-prescribed Linux/x86_64 Alpine `zig build test-tsan` container gate with the checkout copied writable and both Zig caches container-local.

lock-valid? session: Session => Bool.
path-ready? session: Session, item: Module => Bool.
has-match? session: Session, item: Module => Bool.
winner session: Session, item: Module, has-match? session item => Package.
owns-prefix? package: Package, item: Module => Bool.
longer-prefix? left: Package, right: Package => Bool.
store-ready? session: Session, package: Package => Bool.
module-ready? session: Session, package: Package, item: Module => Bool.
resolve session: Session, item: Module => Outcome.
full-name-candidate? session: Session, item: Module => Bool.
package-named? outcome: Outcome => Bool.
module-named? outcome: Outcome => Bool.
sync-guidance? outcome: Outcome => Bool.
network-used? session: Session => Bool.
lock-mutated? session: Session => Bool.
native-loaded? session: Session => Bool.
read-once? session: Session => Bool.
legacy-equivalent? session: Session => Bool.
loading-lease-first? session: Session, item: Module => Bool.
winner-rechecked? session: Session, item: Module => Bool.
bounded-polling? session: Session, item: Module => Bool.
single-publication? session: Session, item: Module => Bool.
---
> Every Session owns exactly one immutable discovery outcome, and absence of the explicit host capability means absence of the tier.
all session: Session | lock-absent? session or lock-invalid? session or lock-valid? session.
all session: Session | lock-absent? session -> ~(lock-invalid? session) and ~(lock-valid? session).
all session: Session | lock-invalid? session -> ~(lock-absent? session) and ~(lock-valid? session).
all session: Session | lock-valid? session -> ~(lock-absent? session) and ~(lock-invalid? session).
all session: Session | ~(project-enabled? session) or ~(host-io? session) -> lock-absent? session.
all session: Session | read-once? session.

> Embedded modules are absolute first priority.
all session: Session, item: Module | embedded? item -> resolve session item = embedded-outcome.

> Invalid locks are deterministic errors for non-embedded names and never open the path tier.
all session: Session, item: Module | ~(embedded? item) and lock-invalid? session -> resolve session item = invalid-lock-outcome.

> An absent lock is observationally the legacy embedded/ECL PATH loader.
all session: Session | lock-absent? session -> legacy-equivalent? session.
all session: Session, item: Module | ~(embedded? item) and lock-absent? session and path-ready? session item -> resolve session item = path-outcome.
all session: Session, item: Module | ~(embedded? item) and lock-absent? session and ~(path-ready? session item) -> resolve session item = undefined-outcome.

> A valid lock selects the longest dotted owner and addresses M4's root-level full canonical filename.
all session: Session, item: Module | lock-valid? session and has-match? session item -> owns-prefix? (winner session item) item and full-name-candidate? session item.
all session: Session, item: Module, package: Package | lock-valid? session and has-match? session item and owns-prefix? package item -> ~(longer-prefix? package (winner session item)).
all session: Session, item: Module | ~(embedded? item) and lock-valid? session and has-match? session item and store-ready? session (winner session item) and module-ready? session (winner session item) item -> resolve session item = locked-outcome.

> Matched names fail closed with actionable, attributable errors.
all session: Session, item: Module | ~(embedded? item) and lock-valid? session and has-match? session item and ~(store-ready? session (winner session item)) -> resolve session item = missing-store-outcome.
all session: Session, item: Module | ~(embedded? item) and lock-valid? session and has-match? session item and store-ready? session (winner session item) and ~(module-ready? session (winner session item) item) -> resolve session item = missing-module-outcome.
all session: Session, item: Module | lock-valid? session and has-match? session item -> resolve session item ~= path-outcome.
package-named? missing-store-outcome.
sync-guidance? missing-store-outcome.
package-named? missing-module-outcome.
module-named? missing-module-outcome.

> Unmatched names alone may use ECL PATH.
all session: Session, item: Module | ~(embedded? item) and lock-valid? session and ~(has-match? session item) and path-ready? session item -> resolve session item = path-outcome.
all session: Session, item: Module | ~(embedded? item) and lock-valid? session and ~(has-match? session item) and ~(path-ready? session item) -> resolve session item = undefined-outcome.

> The runtime is a bounded read-only source consumer and retains the production module-publication protocol.
all session: Session | ~(network-used? session) and ~(lock-mutated? session) and ~(native-loaded? session).
all session: Session, item: Module | loading-lease-first? session item and winner-rechecked? session item and bounded-polling? session item and single-publication? session item.
